comparator.name: Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for the Fall-2026 cohort: the current Dutch-language 'Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid' overview, 'Inhoud' (content) and 'Toekomst' (career) pages; the Faculty of Law's official 2026-2027 'Wijzigingen en overgangsregelingen' (changes and transitional-arrangements) notice; and the most recent full Teaching and Examination Regulations (OER) text for this bachelor obtainable through available tools, studiejaar 2021-2022. Article 10.2 (Opleidingstrajecten en/of afstudeerrichtingen) of that OER records 'n.v.t.': the normalized target cp-000115 (registry row 123, source_provider_id 111A136, recognized_programme_code 50700/CROHO 50700, languages_json=["NLD"]) is the generic Dutch-taught Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid with no formal specialisation route to instantiate, so routeSelection is null. The current 2026-2027 official 'Wijzigingen en overgangsregelingen' notice confirms 'JAAR 1: Geen wijzigingen' and 'JAAR 2: Geen wijzigingen' for this exact target, i.e. the Year-1 and Year-2 compulsory curricula the OER documents remain the current Fall-2026 curriculum unchanged; it reports Year-3 changes only as course-level substitutions inside two of the programme's seven named minors (Minor Algemene Rechtspraktijk: Consumentenrecht discontinued, replaced by a new Rechtshulp Clinic course; Minor Gezin, recht en forensische gedragswetenschappen: one course renamed/replaced), which do not affect the compulsory Year-3 core this decision uses and are not material because no specific minor's content is instantiated (see below). The current official 'Inhoud' page independently corroborates the OER's Year-1 (eleven named units), Year-2 (ten named units, one of which the current page calls 'Arbeidsrecht' where the OER records the identical 6-EC, level-300 unit as 'Sociaal recht' -- the same employment/labour and social-security-law subject matter under the current colloquial name, per the 'Wijzigingen' notice's confirmation that Year 2 is otherwise unchanged) and Year-3 structure (a first-semester free elective/minor followed by Bachelorscriptie, Pleitoefening, Law en Governance, Staatsrecht and Encyclopedie der rechtswetenschap II). Year 1 (Article 11.3, 60 EC, all compulsory, level 100): Beginselen bestuursrecht (6), Beginselen Europees recht (6), Beginselen staatsrecht (6), Beginselen strafrecht (6), Encyclopedie der rechtswetenschap I (6, academische kern), Inleiding goederenrecht (3), Inleiding in de rechtswetenschap (6), Inleiding verbintenissenrecht (6), Juridische vaardigheden (6, academische kern; embeds the PPI-1 professional-identity leerlijn and a compulsory Dutch-language diagnostic taaltoets, neither separately credited), Personen- en familierecht (3), Rechtsgeschiedenis (6, academische kern). Year 2 (Article 11.3, 60 EC, all compulsory, level 300 except Volkenrecht at level 200): Bestuursrecht (6), Burgerlijk procesrecht en insolventierecht (6), Contractenrecht (6), Formeel strafrecht (6), Fundamental Rights in Europe (6; Article 9.1 requires Beginselen staatsrecht and Beginselen Europees recht as entry requirements), Goederenrecht (6), Materieel strafrecht (6), Sociaal recht/Arbeidsrecht (6), Vennootschaps- en rechtspersonenrecht (6), Volkenrecht (6). Year 3 (60 EC): Article 12.1 fixes the first semester as a vrije keuzeruimte (free elective/profiling space) of at least 30 EC, filled by a minor (a pre-set 30-EC package) or an equivalent faculty-approved alternative; Article 12.2 and the current official page confirm the student chooses one of seven current Faculty of Law minors (Algemene Rechtspraktijk; Recht van de toekomst; Fiscaal recht; Law and Global Society: Internet, Migration and Climate Change; Technology, Law and Ethics; Gezin, recht en forensische gedragswetenschappen; Forensische Criminologie) or an approved external/university minor, without prior examination-board approval. No target-specific evidence favours one minor over another, so -- consistent with Section 2.1's instruction to preserve genuine open elective or profiling space explicitly as a curriculum component rather than inventing content for it -- this 30-EC space is recorded as a single generic keuzeruimte/minor component rather than instantiating one specific minor's coursework. The second semester of Year 3 is the fixed compulsory academic core (Article 11.3, level 300): Bachelorscriptie (6; Article 9.1 permits enrolment only after 120 EC including Juridische vaardigheden is completed), Encyclopedie der rechtswetenschap II (6, academische kern), Law en Governance (6, academische kern), Pleitoefening (6; Article 9.1 permits enrolment only after 99 EC including Juridische vaardigheden is completed), Staatsrecht (6). 60 (Year 1) + 60 (Year 2) + 60 (Year 3: 30 keuzeruimte/minor + 30 compulsory core) = 180 EC. No further official source needed to be consulted: the current official overview/content/career pages and the OER together establish a complete, internally consistent, entirely accounted-for 180-EC pathway with explicit EC for every component, current confirmation that Years 1-2 and the Year-3 compulsory core are unchanged for the Fall-2026 cohort, and an explicit, UCR-independent judgment (preserving rather than instantiating the free keuzeruimte/minor) fixed before any UCR course was considered.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's generalist Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid (Article 10.2 confirms no formal afstudeerrichtingen exist for this normalized target): a broad legal education combining UCR's complete available law catalogue -- private law, criminal law, constitutional law, EU law, public international law and human rights -- with UCR's business, company-law, economics, organisational-governance, negotiation and advocacy/communication offerings, reproducing as closely as UCR's catalogue allows the programme's own combination of a compulsory generalist legal core, a Law-and-Governance capstone course, and legal-skills/pleading-practice training, while leaving the 30-EC free elective minor honestly preserved as unclaimed elective space.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines UCR's full available law cluster (7 of 24: Law, Society & Justice and all six GOSLAWJ courses, covering private, criminal, constitutional, EU and international law) with a business/company-law and economics cluster (5 of 24: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Transnational Business Law, Introduction to Economics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics), an organisational-governance and advocacy cluster (5 of 24: International Business & Governance, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Rhetoric in Action, Persuasive Communication), and general social-science/methods breadth (4 of 24: Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Sociology, Qualitative Research Methodology, Theory of International Relations) plus Ethics, The Art of Rhetorical Communication and Personal & Professional Development. The label names law first for the dominant dedicated legal cluster, governance second for the institutional, political and organisational-practice content that recurs throughout the programme's own public-law, company-law and Law-and-Governance components, and legal advocacy third for the negotiation, pleading and persuasive-communication skills that reproduce the programme's own Juridische vaardigheden and Pleitoefening training.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by the generator-eligible programme-interest rows that specifically name 'legal challenges created by new technology' and 'climate law and the climate crisis' as two of the current programme's own headline themes (rows 5271, 5272), independently corroborated by two of the programme's own seven current Faculty of Law minors being organised around exactly this territory (Recht van de toekomst; Law and Global Society: Internet, Migration and Climate Change): a concentration retaining the same compulsory generalist law core but replacing the closest match's business/economics/governance-practice breadth with UCR's sustainability, environmental-governance, climate-communication and technology/AI offerings, studying how law and governance respond to technological disruption and the climate crisis.

The label names law first for the retained dedicated legal core, technology second for the artificial-intelligence, data and platform-governance content, and the climate crisis third for the sustainability, environmental-governance and climate-communication content that together organise this alternative's distinctive academic priorities.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: VU's Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid names 'legal challenges created by new technology' and 'the climate crisis' as two of the current programme's own headline current-affairs themes (evidence rows 5271, 5272), alongside a free 30-EC minor/keuzeruimte in which two of the seven current Faculty of Law minors (Recht van de toekomst; Law and Global Society: Internet, Migration and Climate Change) are explicitly organised around exactly this territory. The closest match reproduces the shared compulsory law core together with UCR's business, economics, organisational-psychology and communication breadth, standing in for the programme's own generalist private-law, company-law, labour-law and advocacy/professional-practice content. This alternative instead retains the identical shared law core (Law, Society & Justice and all six GOSLAWJ courses, plus the shared research-methods, sociology, rhetoric and ethics courses -- 12 of 24 courses) but replaces the closest match's business, economics, organisational-psychology, negotiation, qualitative-methods, political-theory and applied-communication cluster (12 of 24 courses, 90 EC) with UCR's sustainability, environmental-governance, climate-communication, data-science and EU-politics offerings (12 of 24 courses, 90 EC), organised around how law and governance respond to technological disruption and the climate crisis. This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from generalist professional-practice breadth to a technology-and-climate-governance concentration, and the two alternatives share 12 of 24 courses while differing in 12 of 24 each way (90 EC), comfortably exceeding the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

progressionAssessment.rationale: GOSGATE102 (semester 1, no prerequisite) is a formal prerequisite for GOSLAWJ211, GOSLAWJ212, GOSLAWJ213, GOSLAWJ311 and GOSLAWJ312, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. BENGATE101 (semester 1, no prerequisite) precedes BENBUSI311 (semester 4) and BENENTR312 (semester 5), which formally require it. BENGATE102 (semester 2, no prerequisite) precedes BENLEAD311 (semester 3), BENBUSI311 and BENECON311 and BENLEAD312 (semester 4) and BENECON212 (semester 6), which formally require it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory gateway and level-1 courses (Law, Society & Justice, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Sociology, Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Economics, Human Rights: Law & Philosophy) are concentrated in semesters 1, 2 and 5, and level-3 advanced work (Principles of Private Law, Foundations of European Union Law, Transnational Business Law, Public Economics, International Business & Governance, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Persuasive Communication) is concentrated in semesters 3-5, so that foundational orientation precedes advanced applied work where a reasonable sequence is available. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match directly owns twelve generator-eligible rows: how law operates in a complex society and applying legal rules to current social problems (5245, 5246); critically evaluating laws and legal arguments (5247); helping people and organisations with legal questions (5248); finding and interpreting legal sources (5249); oral and written legal advocacy (5250); private law and contracts (5251); criminal law and criminal procedure (5252); constitutional and administrative law (5253); European law and fundamental rights (5254); legal academic research (5274); and legal minors within the bachelor (5273), which documents the existence of the programme's own free 30-EC keuzeruimte/minor mechanism rather than naming an independent substantive direction, and is therefore substantively covered by the core's own preserved elective-space component rather than forced into a residual candidate. The remaining two generator-eligible rows -- legal challenges created by new technology (5271) and climate law and the climate crisis (5272) -- were independently assessed as one coherent candidate direction, 'Law, Technology and the Climate Crisis', additionally supported by illustrative and outcome-trajectory evidence (platform liability for identity fraud, greenwashing, internet law and climate-change/corporate-law master's specialisations). This candidate passes all four gates: it is evidence-backed by two generator-eligible rows that the programme's own current official overview names as headline current-affairs themes, independently corroborated by two of the programme's own seven current Faculty of Law minors being organised around exactly this territory; it has a clear organising logic (how law and governance respond to technological disruption and the climate crisis, replacing the closest match's business/governance-practice breadth rather than its shared law core); it is substantively distinct, replacing 12 of 24 courses (90 EC) with UCR's sustainability, environmental-governance, climate-communication, data-science and EU-politics offerings, materially changing the alternative's academic priorities; and it is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with six distinct level-300 courses and twelve distinct courses (90 EC) each way against the closest match, comfortably meeting the pairwise 30-EC/4-course floor. Production therefore includes it as the second alternative. No generator-eligible evidence remains unassigned after the closest match and this candidate together account for all fourteen generator-eligible rows, so no further candidate direction could be assessed for a third alternative, and production stops at two included alternatives for insufficient remaining evidence rather than a rejected candidate.

notes.text: VU's Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid is a generalist Dutch-law degree combining a continuous public- and private-law core (constitutional, administrative, criminal, EU, international, property, contract and family-adjacent law), a compulsory Law-and-Governance capstone, legal-skills and pleading-practice training, a bachelor thesis, and a genuinely free 30-EC minor. At UCR, students can approach most of this same substantive territory through UCR's complete available law catalogue together with its business, economics, organisational-governance, negotiation and communication courses, but UCR does not teach Dutch civil procedure/insolvency law, inheritance or matrimonial-property law, dedicated administrative-law doctrine, dedicated legal history, or legal-theory/jurisprudence at the depth or in the dedicated form the comparator provides, and it does not reproduce the comparator's own free 30-EC minor space. These pathways therefore compare related legal and civic fields; UCR's programmes approach the comparator's subject matter through UCR's own combination of disciplines rather than reproducing the external law curriculum course by course.

Both the closest match and the technology-and-climate alternative include substantial study of the comparator's shared generalist law core (private, criminal, constitutional, EU and international law). The comparator additionally includes specialist components -- civil procedure/insolvency law, dedicated administrative law, inheritance/family-law depth, legal history and legal-theory/methodology -- that UCR does not offer at any level of depth; UCR students can instead combine adjacent business, economics, governance, communication, sustainability and technology coursework, but those specialist legal components are not offered at the same level of depth or in dedicated form.
